outcome.answer:
Use LLMs to extract semantic profiles or preference triples from user data, then place those profiles into a knowledge graph so they can be propagated and used for recommendation. One approach generates semantic profiles for KG entities with LLMs, integrates them into the KG, and matches LLM-based and KG-based representations during training [1]. Another builds personal knowledge graphs by extracting RDF-compliant user-preference triples from conversational data and shows they can help downstream recommendations [2].

Related papers differ in emphasis: some focus on persona modeling from heterogeneous KGs and LLM-derived item embeddings for session-based recommendation [3], while others use LLMs to create personalized world knowledge or user interest personas and then fuse that knowledge into recommendation systems more carefully [4, 6]. A GraphRAG-based approach also combines historical preferences from a knowledge graph with broader graph communities to create personalized prompts [5].
